messages:
tara: FYI — PR #847 changed the default for request.max_tokens from 1024 -> 512 in staging. Deploy bot flagged it as docs-needed. Is this a patch or a minor? Also need release-note wording and a deploy window.

deploy-bot: automated-check: diff shows only default value changed, API schema unchanged. flag: docs:true. recommended: canary rollout + release note.

nina: Default changes can be sneaky. Any clients that relied on the implicit behavior will see different outputs. I'd argue minor.

alex: Counterpoint — if almost all callers set max_tokens explicitly, it's safe to call it a patch. Do we have telemetry on how often callers omit the field?

maria: Quick check: ~22% of hosted requests in the last 30d omit request.max_tokens (filtered by public endpoints). So it's not negligible.

tj: Given that, I'd lean toward minor. The output distribution can change for those callers. Mitigation: canary + clear release note and an SDK default shim for one release.

nina: +1 for an SDK shim or a feature flag. We should avoid surprising downstream teams. Also add a compatibility label in the changelog so on-call knows to prioritize regression alerts.

tara: Plan proposal: schedule a canary tomorrow 11:00-13:00 PST. Rollout plan: 10% for 30m -> 50% for 30m -> full if metrics look good. Rollback plan: if token-generation latency or failure rate increases by >5% or QA finds quality regressions, revert image and traffic switch. I can open a followup PR to add an opt-out flag in SDKs that keeps old default for one release.

alex: Sounds reasonable. For semver decision — minor. We'll tag the release as minor and annotate the changelog entry with the compatibility notes.

maria: I'll draft the release note now. Proposed blurb:

```
Change: default request.max_tokens reduced from 1024 to 512.
Reason: reduce typical memory/cost for short prompts and align defaults across runtimes.
Impact: callers that do not set max_tokens may see shorter outputs. To preserve previous behavior, set request.max_tokens explicitly to 1024.
Compatibility: non-breaking API schema change; behavior change for callers relying on implicit default.
```

maria: I'll post the draft to the release-notes PR and ping docs for a short note.

tj: Assigning release_note -> maria. I'll add the compatibility label and notify the support rotation to watch for post-deploy issues.

deploy-bot: rollout-schedule created: canary 10% @ 2026-03-21T11:00:00-08:00 PST, health-check: token_failure_rate, latency_p50, output-length-regression. auto-rollback on +5% error or p50 > baseline + 150ms.

tara: Thanks — action items: 1) maria drafts RN + PR, 2) tara opens SDK opt-out PR, 3) nina & alex validate telemetry alerts, 4) tj notifies support. We'll reconvene on this thread once the RN + SDK PRs are up. :thumbsup:
